title: feat: search the items on a shopping list
intent_at_opening: Add a search field to a shopping list that hides non-matching items in place. Matching is delegated to the existing useSearch so it 'ranks and tolerates typos exactly like every other search box in Mealie', over food names, notes, aliases, units and labels.
fix_commit_message: fix(shopping-list): keep the fuzzy tier out of the grouped list filter
bug: useSearch's typo-tolerant fuzzy tier matched unrelated items, which then showed up under their own aisle looking like real hits (e.g. 'cash' matched every wash/stash item, 'milk' matched camomile tea).
evidence: Commit message: "the fuzzy tier turned "cash" into 11 matches (every "wash", "washes" and "stash") and "milk" into 2 (camomile tea, family pack)". Fix passes a zero Fuse threshold so only exact/prefix/word-prefix/substring tiers match; adds regression tests.
steps_to_observe: Open a long shopping list, type 'milk' or 'cash' in the new search field, and see unrelated items (camomile tea, wash...) left visible.
setup_needed: Login; a shopping list with many items (the author used a real 130-item list).
found_by: author (measured against a real list, after opening the PR)
confidence_reason: Behavior is clearly described, but the fix reverses the opening description's explicit promise to tolerate typos, so it is an intent change more than a mistake.
notes: Second in-PR bug found by reviewer: 'Uncheck All Items' / 'Delete Checked' still acted on checked items hidden by the search (data loss risk); fixed in 98b4ed11412a2559d2d74af188679d5a8c3c6af3 together with a redesign of the search toggle.

title: feat: convert between metric/imperial units
intent_at_opening: Let users toggle recipe ingredients between as-written, metric and imperial (US) units, using pint-generated unit data copied to the frontend; only parsed/standardized ingredients are converted.
fix_commit_message: only consider changing units when switching systems
bug: Choosing a unit system also re-stated ingredients that were already written in that system, e.g. '1 pint' became '2 cups' and '4 tablespoons' became '1/4 cup'.
evidence: Code comment added by fix: "An ingredient the author already wrote in cups or tablespoons is passed through untouched, so the boundary cannot restate "4 tablespoons" as "1/4 cup"." Fix adds a customary flag per unit and skips ingredients already in the target system.
steps_to_observe: Open a recipe whose parsed ingredients use US units (e.g. 1 pint, 4 tbsp), open the unit-system menu and pick US; the amounts get rewritten into other US units.
setup_needed: Login; a recipe with parsed ingredients linked to standardized units.
confidence_reason: Bug is inferred from the fix's code comments and diff; there is no report or discussion of it.
notes: Fix committed ~20 minutes before the PR was opened. Later commits ('disable button instead of hiding it', smart rounding) are design changes, not bug fixes.

title: feat: support drag-and-drop images from web
intent_at_opening: Dragging an image from a web page into a recipe step silently failed because the browser drops a URL, not a file. The PR has the server fetch that URL, store it as an asset and link it.
fix_commit_message: support a few more usecases
bug: When the dragged image is wrapped in a link (Google Images, product grids), text/uri-list holds the link's page URL, so the server was asked to fetch a web page instead of the picture. data: and blob: image drops were also silently ignored.
evidence: Fix code comment: "text/uri-list describes whatever was dragged, which for an image inside a link (Google Images, product grids) is the link rather than the picture -- so the markup's wins." Fix: prefer ; handle data: URLs; toast for blob:.
steps_to_observe: Edit a recipe, then drag a thumbnail from a Google Images results tab onto a step's drop zone; the image isn't inserted (wrong URL fetched).
setup_needed: Login; a recipe in edit mode; a second browser tab with an image inside a link; server outbound network access.
confidence_reason: Commit message is vague ('a few more usecases'); the bug is inferred from the new code comments.
notes: Messy history: CodeQL flagged the first HTML-parsing fallback as client-side XSS; the author removed it (0777cf3896690a3395ebe46fde41488f3300ae0a, 'even though it really isn't a security issue') and the fix later re-introduced img extraction with a regex. Earlier 'fix type' commit was type-only.

title: experimental sidebar: respect light theme sidebar overrides
intent_at_opening: An earlier change overrode all light-theme sidebars wholesale. Now custom themes that define sidebar tokens (but not redesign tokens) keep their own colors, and themes defining sidebarRedesign tokens get the redesign palette plus their overrides.
fix_commit_message: coderabbit
bug: The new palette detection scanned the raw custom CSS, including content the theme validator rejects (e.g. a dark-only @media block), so an invalid override could switch the light-mode sidebar away from the redesign palette.
evidence: CodeRabbit: "`usesRedesignSidebarPalette` scans raw CSS, including rejected `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` content." Fix adds validateThemeCssSafely and validates each light CSS layer before palette detection; tests.
steps_to_observe: Enable the experimental sidebar, use light mode, add a custom CSS override containing only a dark-mode @media rule for --color-sidebarBackground; the sidebar falls back to the non-redesign palette.
setup_needed: Experimental sidebar feature flag; a custom theme / custom CSS override with invalid content.
confidence_reason: Clear bot finding applied by the author, but it is a narrow edge case and no human confirmed it visually.
notes: This PR itself fixes a bug reported on #8974 (light custom themes broken by the new sidebar) in a separate follow-up PR rather than inside #8974.

title: sidebar pt. 7: group-aware account drag and drop
intent_at_opening: Rebuild the redesigned sidebar's account list as a react-aria tree and add drag and drop that is group-aware, so accounts can be moved between account groups naturally.
fix_commit_message: coderabbit
bug: Dropping an account 'after' a row whose next account belongs to another sort partition (off-budget or closed) appended the account to the end instead of placing it before the next same-partition sibling.
evidence: CodeRabbit: "`moveAccount` does not find the successor and appends the account instead of placing it before that sibling." Fix filters candidate successors to the dragged account's partition; adds a mixed on/off-budget/closed test.
steps_to_observe: With on-budget and off-budget accounts interleaved in sort order, drag an on-budget account to drop just after another on-budget account; it lands at the end of the list.
setup_needed: Experimental sidebar redesign flag; several on-budget and off-budget accounts.
confidence_reason: Bot finding with a concrete scenario, fixed three minutes later with a matching regression test.
notes: CodeRabbit's comment is on pre-rebase commit 1c90dce13f; buggy_sha is the surviving commit that added accountTreeMoves. Later in the PR a human reviewer reported misaligned headings/chevrons (fixed in 7758465a7ae36165397947bc16e95829de6134f1, visual), and another user reported broken light custom themes, fixed in separate PR #9003.

title: [AI] Migrate create-folders migration to TypeScript
intent_at_opening: Title only: convert the sync-server's create-folders migration file from JavaScript to TypeScript (the description at opening was an empty template).
fix_commit_message: [AI] Preserve migration titles after TypeScript conversion
bug: Renaming the migration file to .ts changed the migration title that the migrate library records in .migrate, so existing servers would see '1694360000000-create-folders.ts' as a new, unapplied migration.
evidence: Fix code comment: "Migration titles are persisted in .migrate. Keep their original .js titles when source files are converted to TypeScript." Fix maps .ts keys to .js titles in the loader; test asserts the .js title.
steps_to_observe: Upgrade an existing self-hosted sync server that already ran create-folders; the migration is treated as new on startup.
setup_needed: Existing self-hosted actual sync-server data directory with migration state.
found_by: author (no prior review comment points at it)
confidence_reason: The mechanism is explicit in the fix, but the real-world effect (re-running an idempotent mkdir migration) is inferred.
notes: A follow-up commit also rejects duplicate normalized titles.

title: feat(ml): optimized model inference
intent_at_opening: Support new optimized ML model exports and lower memory and CPU cost: mmap, bucketed input shapes, and fp16 GPU inference 'as the new models have been optimized for it'. New models are opt-in with MACHINE_LEARNING_MODEL_REVISION=v2.
fix_commit_message: keep precision for fp32 graphs
bug: The 'use f16 for accelerators' commit removed the OpenVINO precision setting (previously default FP32), so OpenVINO GPUs would run the existing fp32 model graphs at fp16 for users still on the default models.
evidence: Fix code comment: "the GPU would otherwise run an fp32 graph at fp16". Fix sets precision=FP32 for OpenVINO when half precision isn't in use; tests parametrized by model revision.
steps_to_observe: Not directly visible; at most subtly different smart-search/face results on an OpenVINO GPU with the default models.
setup_needed: machine-learning container with OpenVINO on an Intel GPU, default (non-v2) models.
confidence_reason: Regression mechanism is confirmed from both diffs; the user impact (accuracy loss) is not demonstrated.
notes: The PR also removed the MACHINE_LEARNING_OPENVINO_PRECISION setting.

title: chore(mobile): enable dead code CI
intent_at_opening: Enable DCM's unused-code check in CI for the mobile app and make the removals needed to pass it, done by hand 'to try to guarantee nothing would break'.
fix_commit_message: Restore accidentally removed test and set mise default
bug: The dead-code removal deleted the only widget test for DownloadTaskTile, which is still used. The test's wrong import made the component look dead.
evidence: Reviewer: "can we keep this test? `DownloadTaskTile` is still in the app (download info page) and this was its only test". Fix restores download_panel_test.dart with the corrected import.
steps_to_observe: Not observable in the app; only lost test coverage.
setup_needed: None (test suite).
confidence_reason: Clearly a mistake the PR introduced and fixed, but a deleted test is borderline as a 'bug' (no product behavior changed).

title: fix(mobile): resume after the app was launched in the background
intent_at_opening: When iOS background-launches the app for uploads, the first user resume was skipped (never paused), so new photos went missing. Fix: expose wasLaunchedInBackground; 'the first resume that finds no pause asks once' and runs a full local sync.
fix_commit_message: check the background launch at the first resume even after a pause
bug: The background-launch flag was only checked when the app had not been paused. If a pause happened before the first resume, only a delta sync ran and photos taken after the background launch could still be missed.
evidence: Reviewer: "I think you want to check `launchChecked` regardless of `wasPaused`". Fix checks the flag on the first resume regardless of pause state and skips only when neither a pause nor a pending full sync.
steps_to_observe: On iOS: let the OS background-launch the app, have it receive a pause before the user opens it, take a photo, open the app; the photo may be missing until next sync.
setup_needed: iOS device with the Immich app, background backup enabled, a server; hard-to-trigger OS lifecycle timing.
confidence_reason: Reviewer comment is terse. The original description deliberately limited the check to 'no pause', so this may be a design change more than a bug, and whether the scenario occurs is unproven.
notes: Native mobile, not a browser bug; included because the rule was to take qualifying PRs in order.

title: fix(ssh): fetch ssh key by fingerprint
intent_at_opening: Title only (body was just an AI-assistance note): look up SSH public keys by fingerprint instead of by content.
fix_commit_message: fix log
bug: A maintainer refactor pushed to the PR renamed SearchPublicKeyByFingerprint to SearchPublicKeyForSSH but left the old name in the SSH server's error log, so failed lookups logged a function that no longer exists.
evidence: Copilot: "This log message names `SearchPublicKeyByFingerprint`, but that function does not exist and this path now calls `SearchPublicKeyForSSH`." Fix is a one-line log label change in modules/ssh/ssh.go.
steps_to_observe: Trigger an SSH key lookup error and read the server log.
setup_needed: Gitea with built-in SSH server; a failing key lookup.
confidence_reason: Unambiguous and introduced by the in-PR refactor; trivial severity.
notes: Bug introduced by a maintainer's cleanup commits, not by the original author.

title: fix(feed): use meaningful lines as comment excerpt
intent_at_opening: Activity-feed comment excerpts (first 200 chars, or first line for review comments) rendered empty or broken when they started with blank lines or markdown structure. Parse the comment as Markdown and pick the first meaningful source line, 'preserving their original Markdown'.
fix_commit_message: fix(feed): render comment excerpts as prose only
bug: Selecting a single source line at write time cut issue-comment excerpts (previously up to 200 characters) down to one line, broke inline markup that spans lines, and left bad excerpts already stored in the database unfixed.
evidence: Fix commit: "Picking one source line at write time regressed issue comments to a single line, broke inline markup spanning lines, and left excerpts already stored in the database unfixed." Fix renders excerpts as prose-only at display time.
steps_to_observe: Post an issue comment whose first line is short and continues on further lines, then open the dashboard activity feed; the excerpt shows only the first line.
setup_needed: Login; a repository with an issue; dashboard feed (or RSS/Atom feed).
found_by: reviewer (human maintainer, who pushed the fix)
confidence_reason: Regression stated explicitly by the maintainer, but the fix also replaced the whole approach, so part of it is a change of design.

title: fix(migrations): stop endless comment paging when migrating from Gitea
intent_at_opening: The issue-comments endpoint ignores page/limit, so the Gitea/Forgejo migrator looped forever on issues with many comments. Keep paging but stop when a page is longer than the limit or repeats the previous page.
fix_commit_message: fix(migrations): detect repeated comment pages by any seen ID
bug: The repeat check compared only the first comment ID of consecutive pages. If that comment was deleted between requests, the whole list was appended again (duplicate comments). An empty page (page size 0 after a failed settings request) didn't end the loop.
evidence: Fix commit: "Comparing only the first ID of consecutive pages appended the rest of the list again when the first comment was deleted between the two requests." Fix tracks all seen IDs and stops on an empty page.
steps_to_observe: Start a repository migration from a Gitea/Forgejo instance (New Migration in the web UI) while a comment on a large issue is deleted; the migrated issue shows duplicated comments.
setup_needed: Login; a source Gitea/Forgejo instance with an issue having >= MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS comments; concurrent deletion (race).
found_by: reviewer (human maintainer, who pushed the fix)
confidence_reason: Author explicitly agreed ('Yep, I missed that one'); the mechanism is clear from the diff.

title: Fixed floating controls in the React post and page editor
intent_at_opening: Keep the React editor bounded by the viewport so long documents scroll under persistent controls, 'with content scrolling behind a transparent header and opaque themed surfaces on its controls'.
fix_commit_message: Fixed opaque editor controls for published posts
bug: The Unpublish and Unschedule header buttons had no opaque background, so document text scrolling under the transparent header showed through them.
evidence: Fix commit: "Address review feedback for Unpublish and Unschedule and cover their themed backgrounds." Diff adds bg-background to both buttons plus acceptance tests for published (light) and scheduled (dark) posts.
steps_to_observe: Open a published post with long content in the React editor and scroll so text passes under the header; text is visible through the Unpublish button.
setup_needed: Admin login; React editor enabled (labs/flag); a published or scheduled post with long content.
found_by: pre-PR review ('Independent standards and spec reviews', likely AI-assisted), applied by the author
confidence_reason: Directly contradicts the explicit 'opaque themed surfaces on its controls' in the description, and the fix is exactly that.

A more severe in-PR regression was fixed later in e951adb781b0af5664188edd11a8ce957b19f61b: the editor height constraint also applied to normal Admin pages, so virtual lists lost their scroll container and stopped loading further pages (category C).

title: Changed the editor to derive pending saves from live content
intent_at_opening: Route the title blur and feature-image changes through the editor's save-policy gate (commitField) so that, on a draft with an invalid staged value, they stay staged instead of sending a save that fails validation and shows the error banner.
fix_commit_message: Fixed pending validation state during editor save retries
bug: After a save was held for validation, a later command for the same content version with a different target (e.g. Schedule with a future date) didn't clear the old hold. The editor kept showing the validation reason instead of 'saving' and hid later errors.
evidence: Fix commit: "A command can validate the same content version with a different target, such as scheduling a future publish date. Retire the prior validation hold when preparation succeeds". Save engine clears the hold; test added.
steps_to_observe: In the React editor, get a draft save held for validation (e.g. future publish time), then Schedule it; the save status keeps showing the validation hold rather than saving/error.
setup_needed: Admin login; React editor; a draft post with a future publish date; possibly a failing network request to see the hidden error.
confidence_reason: The bug is described only in the fix commit and its test. The exact UI symptom is inferred.
notes: Bug lives in a scope expansion added after opening (3ed74b3 'track pending saves in its save engine'). Later commits fix further in-PR issues (autosave lost during repeated reauthentication, stale validation holds).

title: Added the React Cmd-K search modal behind the globalSearchReact flag
intent_at_opening: Move the Cmd-K search modal, shortcut and result navigation from Ember to React behind a Labs flag, keeping Ember's layout and results. Cmd/Ctrl+K is layout-aware, ignored during IME composition, and only active where the sidebar shows.
fix_commit_message: Fixed Cmd-K shortcut edge cases in the React search modal
bug: The global shortcut listener read event.key before checking modifiers, so a keydown with no key (as browser autofill sends) threw inside the document listener on every page with the sidebar. The shortcut could also open search over another dialog, letting a picked result redirect it.
evidence: Fix commit: "a keydown without a key (as autofill sends) threw inside the document listener on every page with the sidebar." Fix checks modifiers first, treats a missing key as none, and blocks the shortcut while another dialog is open.
steps_to_observe: With the flag on, use browser autofill in any Admin form; an uncaught error appears in the console (no visible UI change).
setup_needed: Admin login; globalSearchReact Labs flag enabled; browser autofill data.
confidence_reason: The exception is explicit in the commit, but whether users would notice anything beyond a console error is unclear.
notes: Several later commits are visual/design corrections (hint contrast in light mode, empty results band), some of which are also small in-PR visual bugs.

title: Enhancement: centralized management of share links + bundles
intent_at_opening: Add a central page to manage share links and share-link bundles (screenshot provided); backend changes are minimal (adds document_title to share link responses).
fix_commit_message: Fix table bg
bug: The new share-link and bundle tables inherited the app-wide table style (--bs-table-bg: var(--bs-light-rgb)), so their background didn't match the page.
evidence: Commit message is only "Fix table bg". Diff adds bg-body to both new tables and a CSS rule mapping table.bg-body to --bs-body-bg.

title: Enhancement: parse advanced search with whoosh-compat and delete the handwritten translation
intent_at_opening: Parse advanced-search queries with the whoosh-compat parser and emit Tantivy queries directly, deleting the hand-written translator (closes an issue about v2 Whoosh saved views breaking after upgrade). Description at opening was mostly the PR template.
fix_commit_message: Route SCHEMA_FIELD_MISSING into an error, not an HTTP 400
bug: When the search index schema was missing a field (a stale index after upgrade), the query was answered with HTTP 400 'Field ... is not available', blaming the user's query. This hid a server-side misconfiguration from 5xx monitoring.
evidence: Copilot: "this path logs it and then converts it to `SearchQueryError`, producing HTTP 400. That misclassifies a recoverable server failure as invalid client input and hides it from 5xx monitoring." Fix re-raises (becomes 500).
steps_to_observe: On an install whose search index wasn't rebuilt after upgrade, run an advanced search on a field missing from the index; the UI shows a query error instead of a server error.
setup_needed: Bare-metal/upgraded install with a stale Tantivy index; login; advanced search.
found_by: reviewer (AI bot: Copilot); author agreed ('maybe should be louder')
confidence_reason: The original code documented 400 as deliberate, so the fix reflects a changed decision. Whether it counts as a bug at all is debatable.
notes: Copilot also flagged CJK/fuzzy clauses losing Boolean/field scoping and removed legacy numeric fields; the author deferred those or called them intentional, so they weren't fixed in the PR.

title: Fix: ui version content switching inconsistencies
intent_at_opening: Fix four document-version switching problems: content edits lost on version change (now a dialog with save+proceed), swapped content after leaving and returning, races on quick switching, and false 'unsaved changes' after returning.
fix_commit_message: Prevent dropdown fire on same version
bug: Selecting the already-selected version in the version dropdown opened the new unsaved-content dialog and could discard edits, even though no version change was happening.
evidence: Copilot: "Selecting the already checked version currently enters the unsaved-content dialog and can discard edits even though no version change is occurring." Fix: one-line early return when versionId equals the selected version.
steps_to_observe: Open a document with several versions, edit its content, open the version dropdown and click the version already selected; the unsaved-changes dialog appears and choosing discard loses the edit.
setup_needed: Login; a document with multiple versions.
confidence_reason: The bot's scenario is concrete and the one-line fix matches it exactly. The dialog was added earlier in the same PR (ad9313a2).
notes: Very messy PR: Copilot kept finding race conditions in the new logic through several rounds (stale requests, dirty tracking, save-and-switch race); the author fixed several and then pushed back ('this is getting to be garbage').

title: perf: Render simple read-only comments without an editor view
intent_at_opening: Stop mounting a full ProseMirror view per read-only comment. Simple content (paragraphs, basic marks, emoji, lists) renders from the schema serializer, anything else falls back. Notification comment previews use the same read-only path.
fix_commit_message: fix: Forward className on the static editor path
bug: The new static render path didn't forward className, so styles from wrappers were lost. Notification previews lost their three-line truncation, font size, margins and pointer-event rules.
evidence: Copilot: "`props.className` is not forwarded... notification previews lose their three-line truncation, font size, margin, and pointer-event rules". Fix adds className={props.className} to the static EditorContainer.
steps_to_observe: Have another user leave a long plain-text comment, open the notifications popover; the comment preview is not truncated and is styled differently.
setup_needed: Two users; a document with a plain-text comment generating a notification.
confidence_reason: Concrete bot finding with a one-line matching fix; a behavior-preserving perf refactor is expected not to change looks.

title: perf: Memoize store filter methods with computedFn
intent_at_opening: Memoize document/comment store filter and sort methods with mobx-utils computedFn so they return stable arrays and memoized lists stop re-rendering; public signatures unchanged.
fix_commit_message: perf: Use observable clock for date-filtered store lookups
bug: Memoized date-filtered lookups (deleted documents, drafts) computed their cutoff with new Date(), which MobX doesn't track. Lists would go stale as documents crossed the day/week/month cutoff.
evidence: Copilot: "This cached function depends on `new Date()`, which is not an observable dependency... the list becomes stale." Fix replaces new Date() with mobx-utils now(60000) in both lookups.
steps_to_observe: Keep the Drafts or Trash view with a date filter open across the filter's cutoff time; items that should drop out stay listed until something else changes.
setup_needed: Login; drafts or deleted documents near a date-filter boundary; a long-lived tab.
confidence_reason: The mechanism is clear, but it needs time to pass while the page stays open, so it's rarely observed.
notes: Copilot's other finding (thread lists still returning new arrays) was not addressed in the PR.

title: Adopt React 19 hooks for browser-state and client-side filters
intent_at_opening: Rewrite browser-state hooks (media query, window size, scroll, visibility, persisted state) with useSyncExternalStore, adopt useEffectEvent and useDeferredValue. Public signatures unchanged. Closes an issue listing these refactors.
fix_commit_message: fix: Refresh usePersistedState default when key changes
bug: The rewritten usePersistedState captured its default only on first render. When the key changed (e.g. collection-tab:undefined to the real collection id) and nothing was stored, it returned the old key's default, so the collection page could open on the wrong default tab.
evidence: Copilot: "`defaultValueRef` is captured only on the first render, so it is also reused when `key` changes... this hook still returns the old key's fallback." Fix keeps the default in state and refreshes it on key change.
steps_to_observe: Open a collection (with a description) that you have never opened before; the default tab may be the wrong one because the default derived before the id loaded is kept.
setup_needed: Login; a collection never visited in this browser (no stored tab), with a description.
confidence_reason: Clear regression in hook semantics. The concrete UI symptom comes from the bot's example, not from a repro.
notes: Second commit fixed a type error (JSON.stringify returning undefined), type-only.

title: fix(ui): resolve React 19 ref deprecation warning in Tooltip (#30110)
intent_at_opening: Fix the React 19 'Accessing element.ref was removed' warning in Tooltip by wrapping non-element children safely, and return early when there is no content.
fix_commit_message: fix(ui): preserve numeric tooltip content in Tooltip component guard
bug: The new 'if (!content)' early return treated numeric 0 as empty, so a tooltip whose content is 0 was no longer rendered.
evidence: CodeRabbit: "When `content={0}`, the falsy guard returns `children` before creating the Radix tooltip." Fix checks explicitly for undefined, null or empty string.
steps_to_observe: Hover an element whose Tooltip content is the number 0; no tooltip appears.
setup_needed: Login; a UI spot that passes 0 as tooltip content (unclear whether any exists).
confidence_reason: Mechanism is certain, but it's unclear whether any real tooltip in the app passes 0.
notes: Repository now brands itself Cal.diy.

title: fix: trim whitespace in parseIpFromHeaders to prevent IP banlist bypass
intent_at_opening: parseIpFromHeaders didn't trim whitespace, so a padded x-forwarded-for value could bypass the IP_BANLIST exact match. Add .trim() in both the array and string branches, with tests.
fix_commit_message: fix: address CodeRabbit review feedback
bug: The added rawIp.trim() throws a TypeError when the header value is an empty (or sparse) array, because value[0] is undefined. Before the PR the function just returned undefined.
evidence: CodeRabbit: "`[]` or a sparse array can make `rawIp` undefined and cause a runtime exception". Fix: rawIp?.trim() ?? "" plus an empty-array test (and a test-env cleanup fix).
steps_to_observe: Send a request whose x-forwarded-for header parses to an empty array; the server throws during IP extraction.
setup_needed: Direct HTTP requests with crafted headers; an IP_BANLIST configuration.
confidence_reason: Clear new crash path introduced by the PR's .trim(), though unlikely to be hit in practice.
notes: The same fix commit also corrected a test cleanup that assigned undefined to process.env (which becomes the string 'undefined').

title: fix(bookings): refund all seat payments when cancelling a paid seated…
intent_at_opening: When a paid seated booking is fully cancelled under an automatic refund policy, only the first seat's payment was refunded. Refund every successful, not-yet-refunded payment so all attendees get their refunds.
fix_commit_message: fix(bookings): make seat refunds resilient and drop dayjs in test
bug: The new loop awaited each seat's refund in turn, so one failed provider call aborted the loop and the remaining seats were never refunded, recreating the original under-refund bug.
evidence: CodeRabbit: "If one `handlePaymentRefund` call rejects, the loop aborts and later successful seat payments are never attempted". Fix wraps each refund in try/catch and throws an aggregate error afterwards; test added.
steps_to_observe: Cancel a paid seated booking with several seats while the payment provider fails for one seat; later seats aren't refunded (visible only in the payment provider/DB).
setup_needed: Login as host; a seated event type with payments (e.g. Stripe app) and automatic refund policy; several paid seats; a provider failure.
confidence_reason: Loop introduced by the PR; the failure mode is explicit and fixed with a matching test.

title: FEATURE: Add event summaries to markdown endpoints
intent_at_opening: Markdown endpoints dropped event metadata stored in cooked HTML attributes. Render event summaries with localized labels, timezone-aware dates, formatted descriptions and links, including date-only output for all-day events.
fix_commit_message: FIX: Separate markdown metadata rows with hard breaks
bug: The new event summary joined its metadata rows (Starts/Ends/Location/Link) with plain newlines, so any Markdown renderer merged them into one run-on paragraph.
evidence: Commit title "FIX: Separate markdown metadata rows with hard breaks". Diff joins event fields (and the topic header rows) with a backslash hard break instead of \n, bumps the processor VERSION, and updates specs.
steps_to_observe: Request a topic containing an event at its .md URL and render the Markdown; Starts/Ends/Location/Link collapse onto one line (the raw text in the browser looks fine).
setup_needed: Calendar/events plugin enabled; a topic with an event; markdown endpoint.
confidence_reason: Only a commit title as evidence. The output is mainly for machine/LLM use, and the same commit also changed pre-existing header rows, so bug and polish are mixed.
notes: This fix itself introduced a new bug: the hard-break backslash was appended right after the bare topic URL, which broke the autolink. Fixed two minutes later in b730061412f400ac92aaf605f0809e07e0183783 ('FIX: Keep metadata line breaks outside topic URLs').

title: FEATURE: Add Data Explorer query tools to the MCP server
intent_at_opening: Add MCP tools to fetch saved Data Explorer query definitions (admin-only) and run queries, requiring both a new mcp:data-explorer:read OAuth scope and existing per-query access.
fix_commit_message: return 429 instead of 500 when queryratelimited
bug: When the new run-query tool hit Data Explorer's rate limit, the MCP server's generic error handling turned RateLimiter::LimitExceeded into an HTTP 500 instead of a 429 with Retry-After.
evidence: Commit message: "return 429 instead of 500 when queryratelimited". Diff adds 'rescue RateLimiter::LimitExceeded; raise' in the MCP server so Rails renders 429; spec asserts the Retry-After header and JSON-RPC error body.
steps_to_observe: Call discourse_run_query repeatedly from an MCP client until rate-limited; the server responds 500.
setup_needed: Data Explorer plugin; MCP OAuth client with mcp:data-explorer:read; a user with query access; exceed the rate limit.
found_by: CI/tests (likely): the first commit's spec already expected 429; no review comment mentions it
confidence_reason: Bug is explicit in the commit title. How it was found is inferred.
notes: Fix pushed after the PR was already approved.

title: SECURITY: Filter private topic metadata from board cards
intent_at_opening: Harden board cards against metadata disclosure: replace topic-card MessageBus broadcasts with a metadata-free board_updated signal, and filter group-restricted tag names from the board-show API.
fix_commit_message: Check for SiteSetting.tagging_enabled in CardTopicSerializer.tags to ensure consistent behavior of returning no tags across calls when tagging is disabled.
bug: After the change, the board-show path returned no topic tags when tagging was disabled, but the new fallback path (DiscourseTagging.filter_visible) still returned tags. The same card showed different tags depending on which endpoint serialized it.
evidence: Commit: "ensure consistent behavior of returning no tags across calls when tagging is disabled." Fix adds 'return [] unless SiteSetting.tagging_enabled' to CardTopicSerializer#tags, with specs for enabled/disabled.
steps_to_observe: With tagging disabled, add a tagged topic card to a board: the card response/update shows tags, but reloading the board shows none.
setup_needed: Boards plugin; tagging disabled in site settings; topics that still carry tags; a board.
confidence_reason: Inconsistency is real, but which endpoints hit the fallback path and how visible it is to users is inferred.
notes: Security PR (patch-triage items); backported to 2026.9.

title: test(e2e): run against a local Saleor stack
intent_at_opening: Replace the Saleor-Cloud-dependent e2e suite with one that starts its own Saleor in Docker, builds the dashboard from the working tree and restores a DB dump per test; 'pnpm e2e' is the whole interface; new CI workflow.
fix_commit_message: ci(e2e): address workflow review, add actionlint gate
bug: The new e2e CI workflow built its grep argument with ${GREP:+--grep "$GREP"}, which word-splits a GREP value containing spaces. It also interpolated ${{ matrix.target }} directly into a run: script.
evidence: Reviewer: "Missing quotes:" with an array-based suggestion. Fix commit: "`${GREP:+--grep "$GREP"}` word-splits a value containing a space". Fix builds args as an array and passes matrix values via env.
steps_to_observe: Dispatch the e2e workflow with a grep filter containing a space; the test runner receives split arguments.
setup_needed: GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch with a GREP input.
confidence_reason: Clear shell bug in new CI code, explained in the fix commit. Tooling only.
notes: The PR also introduced and then fixed a broken 'pnpm run actionlint -- -color' invocation that turned the new lint check red (0ae62b4de59aea1bb82cd1dd3afabf23e8dea226).

title: Improve Czech translations
intent_at_opening: Bring the Czech dashboard translation to 100% (2,600 new, ~900 refined strings), with Czech ICU plural rules. 'No source code, messages or UI behavior are touched — translation file only.'
fix_commit_message: Fix Czech ICU placeholders and restore full catalog coverage.
bug: Many new Czech strings used the wrong ICU argument names, e.g. {count} instead of {quantity}, a made-up {displayQuantity}, and dropped {warehouseName}/{methodName}. Czech users lost counts, warehouse names and the Product Doctor summary in messages that previously rendered correctly in English.
evidence: Fix commit: "Broken argument names dropped counts, warehouse names, and the Product Doctor summary." Verified by diffing cs.json: 27 keys mismatched the English placeholders at the PR's first commit, none at base; 8 were corrected by the fix.
steps_to_observe: Switch the dashboard language to Czech, restock/fulfill items on an order, or select items in a list; the message shows no count or warehouse (or falls back).
setup_needed: Staff login; Czech locale; orders/warehouses/products to trigger the affected messages.
found_by: reviewer (maintainer, who pushed the fix with an AI agent)
confidence_reason: Verified by diffing the translation files. The exact runtime rendering (blank vs English fallback) depends on react-intl error handling.
notes: Commit history is odd (the fix commit is authored before a merge commit it sits after). The fix also added 57 newer strings and pretty-printed the file.

title: refactor: migrate Radio and RadioGroup to macaw-ui-next
intent_at_opening: Replace every Material-UI radio with macaw-ui-next (row pickers get a small Radio wrapper because radix renders a fieldset), delete the legacy RadioGroupField, and add stories with interaction tests.
fix_commit_message: fix: radio alignment and spacing after macaw-ui-next migration
bug: After the migration, the postal-code include/exclude radios were vertically centered against their two-line labels instead of the first line. In the order address dialog, the new-address form sat flush against the 'Add new address' option.
evidence: Fix commit: "Postal codes options have a two-line label, so the radio was centered against the whole block instead of the first line." Fix adds the simple-radio-group class and a top margin on the new-address form.
steps_to_observe: Configuration > Shipping zones > open a zone > Postal codes: the radios sit mid-label. Order > edit customer address > choose 'Add new address': the form touches the option.
setup_needed: Staff login; a shipping zone; an order with a customer.
confidence_reason: Visual regressions from a like-for-like component migration, described precisely in the fix commit.
notes: A further 'fix radios' commit (+125) followed without explanation.
